title: LRU Cache Data Structure Selection
question: How would you design an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache with O(1) time complexity for get and put operations? Walk me through your data structure choices and trade-offs.

rubric.name: problem_clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies capacity constraints, concurrency requirements, and expected key/value types.

rubric.name: data_structure_choice
rubric.description: Identifies Hash Map + Doubly Linked List combination and explains why single structures fail O(1) requirement.

rubric.name: time_space_complexity
rubric.description: Correctly derives O(1) time for get/put and O(capacity) auxiliary space complexity.

rubric.name: edge_case_handling
rubric.description: Addresses capacity=1, key updating existing item, evicted node pointers, and missing key handling.

rubric.name: communication_clarity
rubric.description: Communicates pointer manipulation and algorithmic steps verbally in a structured way.

expected_signals: Explains why Hash Map provides O(1) lookup but lacks insertion order tracking
Explains why Doubly Linked List enables O(1) removal/insertion of nodes
Uses dummy head/tail nodes to simplify edge pointer logic
red_flags: Suggests array or single LinkedList yielding O(N) search or deletion
Confuses LRU eviction policy with LFU or FIFO
Fails to state space complexity correctly
follow_up_prompts: Why does a singly linked list fail to provide O(1) node removal even if you hold a pointer to the target node?
How would you adapt this design if multiple threads accessed the cache concurrently?
